methods.label: Opposite pairs and rotations
methods.explanation:
Two opposite faces partition the eight vertices. Since the labels sum to \(36\), every face must sum to \(18\).

Color the vertices black and white so that every edge joins different colors. There are four vertices of each color. Call the black labels \(a,b,c,d\), and call their respective opposite-vertex labels \(a',b',c',d'\). Any two black vertices lie on one face, together with the white partners of the other two black vertices. For example, comparing two face sums gives
\[
a+b+c'+d'=a+c+b'+d',
\]
so \(b-b'=c-c'\). Comparing faces with other shared black vertices in the same way gives
\[
a-a'=b-b'=c-c'=d-d'.
\]
Thus all four opposite pairs have the same positive difference \(k\), and their four smaller labels occupy one color class.

Let \(S\) be the sum of those smaller labels. The larger labels sum to \(S+4k\), so
\[
2S+4k=36,
\qquad S=18-2k.
\]
The four smaller labels are distinct positive integers, so \(S\ge1+2+3+4=10\). Therefore \(1\le k\le4\).

For a fixed difference, the smallest unused number must be paired with the number \(k\) larger. This forces the following pairings:
\[
\begin{aligned}
k=1:&\ (1,2),(3,4),(5,6),(7,8),\\
k=2:&\ (1,3),(2,4),(5,7),(6,8),\\
k=4:&\ (1,5),(2,6),(3,7),(4,8).
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(k=3\), the forced pairs \((1,4),(2,5),(3,6)\) leave \(7\) and \(8\), which cannot be paired. Thus exactly three pairings are possible.

Conversely, each displayed pairing produces valid labelings. Choose either color class for the smaller labels, arrange them on its four vertices, and put each larger partner opposite its smaller partner. Every face contains one endpoint from each pair, with exactly two larger endpoints. Its sum is therefore \(S+2k=18\).

For each pairing there are
\[
2\cdot(4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1)=48
\]
labelings of a fixed cube. These choices neither omit nor repeat a labeling, because its opposite pairs and smaller-label color class are determined by its labels. Altogether there are \(3\cdot48=144\) labelings.

A cube has \(8\cdot3=24\) rotations: choose the image of one vertex, then the image of one of its incident edges. Since every label is different, no nonidentity rotation preserves a labeling. Each arrangement is therefore counted exactly \(24\) times, giving
\[
\frac{144}{24}=\boxed{6},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
